items.title: The final PostgreSQL 14 release is 14.25, and the version is 14.25 because the git tag says so.
As of 13:26 UTC the release had NOT shipped. ftp.postgresql.org/pub/source/v14.25/ → 404, postgresql.org/docs/release/14.25/ → 404, the news archive's newest item is still 2026-10-15 (PG 19 RC 1)…
"This is the final release of PostgreSQL 14. PostgreSQL 14 is now end-of-life and will no longer receive security and bug fixes." That is what breaks: nothing stops working today, but every future…
This final release is bug-fix only — no CVEs — but it has the longest post-update checklist in recent memory.
Two more post-update actions that are not reindexes.
The scariest single fix: parallel pg_dump against a standby could corrupt both the dump output and the standby's own data.
The planner's join-removal implementation was rewritten in a minor release.
Three correctness fixes that matter if you rely on isolation guarantees.
Crash-recovery data loss fixed, and prepared-transaction state files are now written atomically.
tzdata 2026f ships in this release — this is the one that closes Cuba.
RC 2 ships today; GA is planned for 2026-11-19, "unless an issue is discovered that requires a delay or an additional release candidate." RC 2 is described as "mostly identical to the initial…
Two hard pg_upgrade blockers you should test for now, not on the 19th. pg_upgrade will refuse a cluster that has btree_gist inet/cidr indexes — the default opclasses moved to GiST because the old…
Three defaults change in ways that will move your numbers. max_locks_per_transaction default goes 64 → 128 and "effectively settings must now be doubled to match their capacity in previous releases"…
Auth gets stricter: RADIUS is removed outright ("PostgreSQL only supported RADIUS over UDP, which is unfixably insecure"), successful MD5 password authentication now logs a warning…
REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) is the headline feature and it replaces VACUUM FULL/CLUSTER without an AccessExclusive lock, using a new max_repack_replication_slots.
Planner and observability changes worth benchmarking: aggregation can now happen before joins (eager aggregation), NOT IN can become an ANTI JOIN when NULLs are absent, parallel TID range scans…
Replication: a WAIT command for read-your-writes off a standby, and logical replication of sequences.
If you tested RC 1, you may have created objects that break the upgrade.
Two vendor surfaces disagree about whether PG 19 needs a reindex after pg_upgrade.
pgvector CVE-2026-103484, CVSS 8.8 — and there is no reachable fix on any of the three big managed Postgres services.
That pgvector fix shipped with a release note reading "Version bump to 0.8.7 [skip ci]".
PgBouncer 1.26.1 fixes THREE CVEs, not the one that got attention — upgrade, don't just read the headline.
The PgBouncer DoS precondition is the configuration almost everyone runs.

What this means for Postgres hosts specifically: your database engine is not exposed, your Alpine-based jump boxes and sidecars are.
